title: SIM registration guidance
text: All SIMs should be registered before activation. The registration flow should ask for the subscriber's full name, date of birth, address, government ID type and ID number, plus a clear photo of the ID. Corporate accounts should be handled by an authorized representative. The purpose of the policy is to keep mobile services tied to a verified identity and reduce scam abuse.
provenance_note: Paraphrased from public SIM registration guidance and FAQs.

title: Prepaid load and billing behavior
text: Prepaid mobile service uses credit that is bought in advance, while postpaid service is billed after the monthly cycle based on actual usage. A telco help article should explain how load purchase, promo activation, and billing cutoffs affect customer experience. Support teams should also be able to explain why a prepaid line may stop working after its balance or promo expires.
provenance_note: Paraphrased from public rules on prepaid and postpaid service behavior.

title: Postpaid billing and account support
text: A postpaid customer may ask why a bill is higher than expected. The support workflow should check plan inclusions, roaming usage, add-on services, overage charges, and the billing cycle cut-off date. If the customer is part of a business account, the authorized representative should handle billing questions and service changes.
provenance_note: Based on public telco help-center patterns for billing and account management.

title: Fiber installation scheduling
text: A fiber install request usually needs an address check, an appointment window, and a site readiness review before the technician visit. If the building is not ready or the line path is blocked, the install may be rescheduled. For a customer-facing knowledge base, the article should distinguish between order submission, appointment confirmation, and activation after installation.
provenance_note: Synthetic telco operations note informed by public fiber and enterprise connectivity offerings.

title: Roaming and travel usage
text: Traveling customers often need to know whether roaming is active, which add-on applies, and how data charges will be billed outside the home network. The guide should explain that roaming may require prior activation or an eligible promo. It should also remind users to check their account balance, plan inclusions, and destination country before travel.
provenance_note: Paraphrased from public roaming and mobile-service help pages.

title: Enterprise extension SIM onboarding
text: Enterprise SIM onboarding should capture the company name, authorized representative, proof of address, and the mobile lines covered by the account. The process is different from consumer prepaid signup because the telco is dealing with a business subscriber and account-level service requirements. A support answer should distinguish company-owned SIMs from personal lines used by employees.
provenance_note: Paraphrased from public enterprise SIM registration and account FAQs.

title: Service outage incident update
text: Network monitoring detected a temporary service interruption in one service area. The incident update should note the affected region, the start time, the service impact, the current restoration status, and the next update time. Customer service should use the same incident summary when answering calls, chat, or email follow-ups.
provenance_note: Synthetic internal-style incident record for QA generation and troubleshooting prompts.

title: Store and support queue handoff
text: If a customer issue cannot be resolved online, the case should be handed off to a store or service desk with the customer's account summary, device details, and the exact troubleshooting steps already attempted. The handoff note should make it clear whether the case is about billing, activation, installation, device replacement, or network quality. This helps the next agent continue without repeating the same questions.
provenance_note: Synthetic workflow note for multi-turn dialogue and troubleshooting generation.
